title: Accordion
description: Rows that fold and unfold. They touch while closed; an open row lifts out on a spring.

blocks.text: ## Installation
manual
**Install the following dependencies:**
**Copy and paste the following code into your project.**

**The springs come from CSS variables. Add them to your CSS file (see `--spring-bouncy` and `--spring-soft` in `app/globals.css`).**





## Usage

blocks.code:
<Accordion defaultValue={["item-1"]}>
  <AccordionItem value="item-1">
    <AccordionTrigger>Is it accessible?</AccordionTrigger>
    <AccordionContent>
      Yes. It adheres to the WAI-ARIA design pattern.
    </AccordionContent>
  </AccordionItem>
</Accordion>

blocks.text: ## Composition

blocks.code:
Accordion
├── AccordionItem
│   ├── AccordionTrigger   (icon, meta)
│   └── AccordionContent
└── AccordionItem
    ├── AccordionTrigger
    └── AccordionContent

blocks.text:
## Icon and value

Give `AccordionTrigger` an `icon` (a glass icon, 22px) and a `meta` value. The content indents to the title, and the value gives way to the content while the row is open, so each fact is shown once.

## Inset

Inside a card or a sheet use `variant="inset"`: the rows step up one level to `field`, as every block inside `card` does.

## Multiple

Use the `multiple` prop to let several rows stay open.

## Disabled

Use `disabled` on `AccordionItem`. The row is dimmed and has no hover.

## Design

- **Shape.** Closed rows share rounded ends: only the first row's top and the last row's bottom are round, and so are the corners facing an open row. An open row lifts out with 10px gaps and a 20px radius on all four corners.
- **Depth.** No borders. The rows are `card` on the page and `field` inside a card (`variant="inset"`). Hover steps the row towards `knob`.
- **Motion.** Height, margins and radii run on the bouncy spring (`--spring-bouncy`, about 11% overshoot). The chevron turns on the soft spring (`--spring-soft`). The head value blurs out and slides 8px right. Reduced motion shortens every transition.
- **Keyboard.** Arrow keys, Home and End move between triggers, Enter and Space toggle a row.

## API Reference

| Part | Prop | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Accordion` | `variant` | `"default"` (on the page) or `"inset"` (inside a card). |
| `Accordion` | `multiple` | Let several rows stay open. Default `false`. |
| `Accordion` | `value`, `defaultValue`, `onValueChange` | The open rows, as an array of item values. |
| `AccordionItem` | `value`, `disabled` | The row's value, and whether it ignores interaction. |
| `AccordionTrigger` | `icon` | A leading icon. The content indents to the title. |
| `AccordionTrigger` | `meta` | A value at the end of the row, hidden while the row is open. |

The rest follows [Base UI](https://base-ui.com/react/components/accordion#api-reference).

<Alert variant="bad">
  <AlertIcon>

blocks.text: ## Composition

blocks.code:
Alert
├── AlertIcon          (a glass icon, 36px)
├── AlertTitle
├── AlertDescription
└── AlertAction        (a button, centred against both lines)

blocks.text:
## Tones

The tone is a state, never decoration. `ok` says things are fine, `warn` asks for attention, `bad` marks an end. The default is a quiet card.

## Line icon

A line icon placed directly in the `Alert` takes the tone's colour and is centred against both lines. Prefer a glass icon in `AlertIcon` for notices the person has to act on.

## Action

Use `AlertAction` to put a button beside the text. It uses the `soft` button; the tone stays on the notice.
## Title only

## Design

- **Shape.** Radius 24, padding `14 18 14 14`, gap 14. The title is 15/22 at 500, the line under it 14/20 in the secondary text colour. The line adds to the title and never repeats it.
- **Tone.** A tint of the card (10%) and a 1px inset ring of the same colour (22%). No border and no shadow.
- **Placement.** One notice per page, above the columns and 22px above them. Say a state once, where it matters.
- **Motion.** A notice that comes blurs in on the soft spring (`notice-in`). Reduced motion drops the travel.
- **Role.** The notice has `role="alert"`, so a screen reader announces it when it appears.

## API Reference

| Part | Prop | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Alert` | `variant` | `"default"`, `"ok"`, `"warn"` or `"bad"`. `"destructive"` is the same as `"bad"`. |
| `AlertIcon` | `className` | A 36px box for the icon. A glass icon takes `size-9`; a line icon is drawn at 18px. |
| `AlertTitle` | `className` | The title. |
| `AlertDescription` | `className` | The line under the title. |
| `AlertAction` | `className` | An action placed at the end of the notice. |

      <AlertDialogDescription>
        The router will forget its key.
      </AlertDialogDescription>
    </AlertDialogHeader>

├── AlertDialogTrigger
└── AlertDialogContent
    ├── AlertDialogHeader

    │   ├── AlertDialogTitle
    │   └── AlertDialogDescription
    └── AlertDialogFooter
        ├── AlertDialogCancel
        └── AlertDialogAction

blocks.text:
## Tones

The icon says what kind of question it is, and the action button agrees with it. A removal has a `red` glass trash and a `red` action. A step that costs something, like Reconnect, has an `orange` icon and an accent button.
A plain choice can use `blue`.

## Without an icon

`AlertDialogMedia` is optional. The title then sits at the top.

## Design

- **Sheet.** The same as [Dialog](/docs/dialog): `card`, radius 36, padding 24 and the sheet shadow. A drawer on a phone and a dialog popping up from its centre from 760px, with the same timings.
- **Question.** Left-aligned, with 24px at the top. A 64px glass icon, a 20/28 title at 500 and a 15/21 paragraph in the secondary text colour.
- **Buttons.** Two equal buttons in a row, default size. **Cancel** is `soft`. The action is `accent`, or `red` for a removal. There is no × beside them.
- **Has to be answered.** A press on the scrim does not close it. A button or Escape does.
- **Action.** `AlertDialogAction` closes the dialog and runs `onClick`. To keep it open while something runs, control it with `open` and `onOpenChange` and give the button `loading`.

## API Reference

| Part | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `AlertDialog` | The root. Controlled with `open` and `onOpenChange`, or `defaultOpen`. |
| `AlertDialogTrigger` | Opens the dialog. Draw it as a `Button` with `render`. |
| `AlertDialogContent` | The sheet and its scrim. |
| `AlertDialogHeader`, `AlertDialogTitle`, `AlertDialogDescription` | The question. |
| `AlertDialogMedia` | A 64px box for a glass icon. |
| `AlertDialogFooter` | A row of equal buttons. |
| `AlertDialogCancel` | Closes the dialog. A `soft` button by default. |
| `AlertDialogAction` | Closes the dialog. An `accent` button by default; takes the Button's `variant` and `size`. |

See the [Base UI](https://base-ui.com/react/components/alert-dialog#api-reference) documentation for the rest.

## Features - Icon and image media through `AttachmentMedia` - Upload states: `idle`, `uploading`, `processing`, `error`, and `done` with built-in styling and a shimmer while in progress - Three sizes and horizontal or vertical orientation - A full-card `AttachmentTrigger` that opens a link or dialog while the actions stay independently clickable - Scrollable, snapping `AttachmentGroup` with an edge fade - Customizable styling through the `className` prop on every part ## Image Set `variant="image"` on `AttachmentMedia` and render an `` inside it. Use `orientation="vertical"` to stack the media above the content.

## States

Set `state` to reflect the upload lifecycle. `uploading` and `processing` shimmer the title, and `error` switches to a destructive treatment.

## Sizes

Use `size` to switch between `default`, `sm`, and `xs`.

## Group

Wrap attachments in `AttachmentGroup` to lay them out in a horizontally scrollable, snapping row with an edge fade.

## Trigger

Add an `AttachmentTrigger` to make the whole card open a link or dialog. It fills the card behind the actions, so the actions stay clickable.

blocks.code:
<Dialog>
  <Attachment>
    {/* media, content, actions */}
    <DialogTrigger
      render={<AttachmentTrigger aria-label="Preview research-summary.pdf" />}
    />
  </Attachment>
  <DialogContent>{/* ... */}</DialogContent>
</Dialog>

blocks.text:

`AttachmentAction` renders a `Button`, and `AttachmentTrigger` renders a real `<button>` (or your element via `render`). Follow the guidance below so both are operable and announced.

### Label icon-only actions

`AttachmentAction` is usually icon-only, so give each one an `aria-label` describing the action and its target.

### Label the trigger

`AttachmentTrigger` covers the card with no text of its own, so give it an `aria-label` for what activating it does.

<AttachmentTrigger
  render={
    <a
      href={url}
      target="_blank"
      rel="noreferrer"
      aria-label="Open workspace.png"
    />
  }
/>

title: Badge
description: A small pill that names a state, and a tile for a store or an action.

blocks.text: ## Installation
manual
**Install the following dependencies. The badge has no state and no ``use client``, so it renders on the server.**
**Copy and paste the following code into your project.**
## Usage

## Variants

The tone is state, never decoration. `default` (the accent) is the plain one, like the Demo chip. `ok` means fine, `warn` needs attention and `bad` is an end. Each is a tint of its colour with the colour as text, and none has a border. `soft` is for a count or a quiet label.

`tint` is the same as `default`, `secondary` is `soft` and `destructive` is `bad`, so code written for shadcn/ui keeps working.

## Sizes

The default is 26px high with 13px text. `sm` is 20px with 11.5px text, for a count beside a word.

## With icon

Mark the icon with `data-icon="inline-start"` or `"inline-end"`. The padding on that side gets smaller.
## With spinner

## Link and button

Use `render` to draw the badge as a link or a button. It then presses to 0.95 and its tint deepens on hover: accent 13% to 20%, warn and ok 14% to 22%. This is how the Update pill works.

## Badge tile

The larger badge is a tile: 60px high with an inverted 36px icon tile, a small line over a main line, and a trailing mark (a chevron for an action, an open mark for a page in a new tab). `primary` on the icon tints it with the accent: use it for the one thing to tap in a step. The tile takes the sheet's `inset` step when it sits inside an inset row.
Two tiles can sit side by side without the trailing mark: a 32px icon tile and 10px padding.

## Design

- **Chip.** A pill, 26px high, padding 12px, gap 6px, 13px at 600. The fill is the tone at 13 or 14% over the surface and the text is the tone itself. Nothing is drawn around it.
- **Interactive.** `render` makes it a link or a button: `scale(.95)` on 200ms ease-out and a deeper tint on hover. Focus is a 2px accent ring at 65%, 2px outside the pill.
- **Tile.** `field`, radius 18, padding `0 14 0 12`, gap 12. The icon tile is radius 10, `text` fill with a `raised` mark. Hover goes one step up to `knob` and a press takes it to 0.98.

## API Reference

| Part | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `Badge` | The chip. `variant` is `"default"`, `"ok"`, `"warn"`, `"bad"`, `"soft"`, `"outline"`, `"ghost"` or `"link"`; `size` is `"default"` or `"sm"`. `render` draws it as another element. |
| `BadgeTile` | The tile. `inset` steps its fill up inside an inset row. `render` draws it as a link or a button. |
| `BadgeTileIcon` | The 36px icon tile. `primary` tints it with the accent. |
| `BadgeTileText`, `BadgeTileLabel` | The two lines: the small label first, then the main line as text. |

blocks.text:
The `Bubble` component displays framed conversational content. Use it for chat text, short structured output, quoted replies, suggestions, and reactions.

For full-featured chat interfaces, use the [`Message`](/docs/components/message) component. `Bubble` is intentionally scoped to the bubble surface. Place avatars, names, timestamps, metadata, and message-level actions in [`Message`](/docs/components/message).

## Installation
cli
manual
**Copy and paste the following code into your project.**

**Update the import paths to match your project setup.**





## Usage

blocks.code: I checked the registry output and removed the stale route. 👍

blocks.text:
## Composition

Use the following composition to build a bubble:
Use `BubbleGroup` to group consecutive bubbles from the same sender:

## Features

- Seven visual variants, from a strong primary bubble to unframed ghost content
- Start and end alignment for sender and receiver bubbles
- Reactions that anchor to the bubble edge with configurable side and alignment
- Bubbles size to their content, up to 80% of the container width
- Polymorphic content via `render` for link and button bubbles
- Customizable styling through the `className` prop on every part

## Variants

Use `variant` to change the visual treatment of the bubble.

| Variant       | Description                                            |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `default`     | A strong primary bubble, usually for the current user. |
| `secondary`   | The standard neutral bubble for conversation content.  |
| `muted`       | A lower-emphasis bubble for quiet supporting content.  |
| `tinted`      | A subtle primary-tinted bubble.                        |
| `outline`     | A bordered bubble for secondary or rich content.       |
| `ghost`       | Unframed content for assistant text or rich content.   |
| `destructive` | A destructive bubble for error or failed actions.      |

A bubble sizes to its content, up to 80% of the container width. The `ghost` variant removes the max-width so assistant text and rich content can span the full row.

## Alignment

Use `align` on `Bubble` to align the bubble to the start or end of the conversation.

| align   | Description                                        |
| ------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| `start` | Align the bubble to the start of the conversation. |
| `end`   | Align the bubble to the end of the conversation.   |

**Note:** When building chat interfaces, you probably want to use alignment on the `Message` component itself, not the `Bubble` component. You can use the `role` prop on the `Message` component to automatically align the bubble to the start or end of the conversation.

## Bubble Group

Use `BubbleGroup` to group consecutive bubbles from the same sender. Note the `align` prop should be set on the `Bubble` component itself, not the `BubbleGroup` component.

## Links and Buttons

You can turn a bubble into a link or button by using the `render` prop on `BubbleContent`.

## Reactions

Use `BubbleReactions` for bubble reactions. You can use it to display reactions or quick action buttons. Use `side` and `align` to position the row — `side="top"` anchors it to the upper edge. Reactions overlap the bubble edge, so leave vertical space between rows — the examples below use a larger `gap` for this reason.

## Show More / Collapsible

Long bubble content can be composed with [`Collapsible`](/docs/components/collapsible) to allow for a show more or show less interaction. Use the `CollapsibleTrigger` component to trigger the collapsible content.

## Tooltip

Wrap a bubble in a [`Tooltip`](/docs/components/tooltip) to reveal metadata on hover, such as when a message was read.

## Popover

Pair a bubble with a [`Popover`](/docs/components/popover) to surface more information on demand, such as the full error message for a failed action.

## Accessibility

`Bubble` renders the presentational message surface. Keep conversation-level semantics on the surrounding container and follow the guidelines below.

### Labeling Reactions

Reactions render as a row of emoji. A screen reader reads each glyph with no context, and counters like `+8` are announced as "plus eight". Group the row as a single image with a descriptive `aria-label` so it announces once. `role="img"` also hides the individual emoji from assistive tech, so no `aria-hidden` is needed.

blocks.code: 👍 🔥 +8

blocks.text: When reactions are interactive, render buttons instead and give icon-only buttons an `aria-label`.

### Interactive Bubbles

When a bubble is clickable, render it as a real `<button>` or `<a>` with the `render` prop so it is focusable and exposes the correct role. `BubbleContent` ships a visible focus ring for interactive elements, and the accessible name comes from the bubble text. No extra label is needed.

blocks.code:
<Bubble variant="muted" align="end">
  <BubbleContent render={<button type="button" onClick={onReply} />}>
    I forgot my password
  </BubbleContent>
</Bubble>

blocks.text:
### Meaning Beyond Color

Bubble variants signal role and tone with color. Pair them with text, alignment, or icons so meaning is not conveyed by color alone. For a `destructive` bubble, keep the error context in the message text rather than relying on the color treatment.

## API Reference

### Bubble

The root bubble wrapper.

| Prop        | Type                                                                                       | Default     | Description                                      |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| `variant`   | `"default" \| "secondary" \| "muted" \| "tinted" \| "outline" \| "ghost" \| "destructive"` | `"default"` | The bubble visual treatment.                     |
| `align`     | `"start" \| "end"`                                                                         | `"start"`   | The inline alignment of the bubble.              |
| `className` | `string`                                                                                   | -           | Additional classes to apply to the root element. |

### BubbleContent

The bubble content wrapper.

| Prop        | Type                       | Default | Description                                               |
| ----------- | -------------------------- | ------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `render`    | `ReactElement \| function` | -       | Render the content as a different element such as a link. |
| `className` | `string`                   | -       | Additional classes to apply to the content element.       |

### BubbleReactions

Displays overlapped reactions for a bubble.

| Prop        | Type                | Default    | Description                                      |
| ----------- | ------------------- | ---------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| `side`      | `"top" \| "bottom"` | `"bottom"` | The side of the bubble to anchor the reactions.  |
| `align`     | `"start" \| "end"`  | `"end"`    | The inline alignment of the reactions.           |
| `className` | `string`            | -          | Additional classes to apply to the reaction row. |

### BubbleGroup

Groups consecutive bubbles from the same sender.

| Prop        | Type     | Default | Description                                    |
| ----------- | -------- | ------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `className` | `string` | -       | Additional classes to apply to the group root. |

title: Button
description: A pill that shrinks under a press. One primary action, quiet and destructive ones, and a busy state with the orb.

blocks.text: ## Installation
manual
**Install the following dependencies. The button has no state and no `use client`, so it renders on the server and `buttonVariants` can be called there.**
**Copy and paste the following code into your project.**

**Add the busy state's CSS (the `data-slot="button-orb"` rules and the `orb-*` keyframes) and the easings to your CSS file. They are in `app/globals.css`.**



**Optional: mount `PressFootprint` once in the root layout (`components/press-footprint.tsx`, the only client part). A press shrinks the button, and a click let go near its edge is still a click.**





## Usage

## Variants

`accent` is the one primary action on a screen: Add this device, Reconnect, Download. `tint` is a quiet primary, like a card's Connect. `soft` is for Cancel, Copy and Start over. `red` is for Remove. Use buttons and pills for actions: never blue text links.

`default` is `accent`, `secondary` is `soft` and `destructive` is `red`, so code written for shadcn/ui keeps working. `outline` and `ghost` are quiet fills without a border; `link` is only for a link inside a sentence.

## Sizes

The default is 48px high, `sm` is 40px, `xs` is 32px (a pill beside a label, like Update) and `lg` is 56px.

## Icon

The round buttons are knobs: a 32px circle (`icon`) with a 16px icon. They scale to 0.8 under a press. `icon-lg` is 40px, `icon-sm` 28px and `icon-xs` 24px. Give them an `aria-label`.

## With icon

An icon goes before or after the words; the padding on that side gets smaller.

## Loading

Pass `loading` while the button waits for an answer. The button keeps its size, its content blurs away and the orb comes up through the blur in the button's own colour. The button stays focusable and ignores clicks meanwhile. It needs no client code: loading is a plain prop, so the button renders on the server too.
## Disabled
## Full width

## As a link

Use `render` to draw the button as another element, and set `nativeButton={false}` when it is not a `<button>`. `buttonVariants` gives the classes alone.

## Design

- **Shape.** A pill: 48px high, 20px padding, an 18px icon, 16/22 text at 500 (600 on accent, tint and red) with -0.015em tracking. No ellipsis on a button: "Remove", never "Remove...".
- **Press.** `scale(.95)` on 200ms ease-out (`--ease-out`). Knobs scale to 0.8 on 150ms.
- **Hover.** accent goes to 82%, tint to 20% (24% pressed) and soft to +6% of the text colour (+10% while it holds an open menu). All on 200ms.
- **Busy.** The content goes out in 180ms ease-in (`blur 5px`, `scale .86`). The orb comes in 70ms later over 340ms ease-out and is not drawn at all (its loop is stopped) while the button is not waiting. It is Orbs B4 Converge from aicss.dev: one dot walks a triangle and a second breathes in the middle, 1.8s loops.
- **Focus.** A 2px accent ring at 65%, 2px outside the pill, only while the keyboard moves focus.
- **Reduced motion.** Transitions shorten and the orb loop stops moving.

## API Reference

| Prop | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `variant` | `"accent"` (or `"default"`), `"tint"`, `"soft"` (`"secondary"`), `"red"` (`"destructive"`), `"outline"`, `"ghost"`, `"link"`. |
| `size` | `"default"`, `"sm"`, `"xs"`, `"lg"`, `"icon"`, `"icon-lg"`, `"icon-sm"`, `"icon-xs"`. |
| `loading` | Waiting for an answer. Shows the orb and ignores clicks. Leave it out for a plain button. |
| `render`, `nativeButton` | Draw the button as another element. See [Base UI](https://base-ui.com/react/components/button#api-reference). |

## About

The `Calendar` component is built on top of [React DayPicker](https://react-day-picker.js.org).

You can use the `<Calendar>` component to build a date picker. See the [Date Picker](/docs/components/base/date-picker) page for more information.

blocks.text:
## Selected Date (With TimeZone)

The Calendar component accepts a `timeZone` prop to ensure dates are displayed and selected in the user's local timezone.

**Note:** If you notice a selected date offset (for example, selecting the 20th highlights the 19th), make sure the `timeZone` prop is set to the user's local timezone.

**Why client-side?** The timezone is detected using `Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().timeZone` inside a `useEffect` to ensure compatibility with server-side rendering. Detecting the timezone during render would cause hydration mismatches, as the server and client may be in different timezones.

## Basic

A basic calendar component. We used `className="rounded-lg border"` to style the calendar.

## Date and Time Picker

## Size

`size="sm"` tightens the spacing to 16px and the radius to 24.

## Spacing

The inset of every part and the gap between them is the `--card-spacing` variable: 20px by default, 16px for `sm`. Set it on the card to change it.

Use `-mx-(--card-spacing)` to let content run edge to edge. A block that steps up to `bg-field` reads as a layer inside the card. When it sits above a footer, put `-mb-(--card-spacing)` on `CardContent` to remove the gap.

## Image

An image before the header sits at the top edge, with the card's radius.

## Design

- **Surface.** `card` (the raised step) with radius 28. There is no ring and no shadow: depth comes from the brightness ladder alone.
- **Layers.** What sits in a card steps up. `CardFooter` is a `field` strip with no border.
- **Text.** The title is 16/22 at 500 with -0.02em. The description is 13/18 in the secondary colour.
- **Nesting.** An inner block has the card's radius minus the space around it: 28 less 8 is 20.

| `CardAction` | Puts a button or a badge at the top right of the header. |

title: Chart
description: Beautiful charts. Built using Recharts. Copy and paste into your apps.

blocks.text: **Updated:** The `chart` component now uses Recharts v3. If you're upgrading existing chart code, see [Updating to Recharts v3](#updating-to-recharts-v3).

Introducing **Charts**. A collection of chart components that you can copy and paste into your apps.

Charts are designed to look great out of the box. They work well with the other components and are fully customizable to fit your project.

[Browse the Charts Library](/charts).

## Component

We use [Recharts](https://recharts.org/) under the hood.

We designed the `chart` component with composition in mind. **You build your charts using Recharts components and only bring in custom components, such as `ChartTooltip`, when and where you need it**.

We do not wrap Recharts. This means you're not locked into an abstraction. When a new Recharts version is released, you can follow the official upgrade path to upgrade your charts.

**The components are yours**.

## Updating to Recharts v3

If you're updating older chart code to Recharts v3:

- Use `var(--chart-1)` instead of `hsl(var(--chart-1))` when you reference chart tokens from your CSS variables.
- Use `ChartTooltip.defaultIndex` for initial tooltip state only. Keep persistent active shapes in your own chart state.
- Remove `layout` from `<Bar>` when the parent `<BarChart>` already defines it.
- Keep a height, `min-h-*`, or `aspect-*` on `ChartContainer` so `ResponsiveContainer` can measure on first render.

## Installation
cli
manual
**Install the following dependencies:**
**Copy and paste the following code into `components/ui/chart.tsx`.**
**Add the following colors to your CSS file**

## Your First Chart

Let's build your first chart. We'll build a bar chart, add a grid, axis, tooltip and legend.



**Start by defining your data**


The following data represents the number of desktop and mobile users for each month.
**Note:** Your data can be in any shape. You are not limited to the shape of the data below. Use the `dataKey` prop to map your data to the chart.

blocks.title: components/example-chart.tsx
blocks.code:
const chartData = [
  { month: "January", desktop: 186, mobile: 80 },
  { month: "February", desktop: 305, mobile: 200 },
  { month: "March", desktop: 237, mobile: 120 },
  { month: "April", desktop: 73, mobile: 190 },
  { month: "May", desktop: 209, mobile: 130 },
  { month: "June", desktop: 214, mobile: 140 },
]

blocks.text:
**Define your chart config**


The chart config holds configuration for the chart. This is where you place human-readable strings, such as labels, icons and color tokens for theming.

blocks.title: components/example-chart.tsx

blocks.text:
**Build your chart**


You can now build your chart using Recharts components.
**Important:** Remember to set a `min-h-[VALUE]` on the `ChartContainer` component. This is required for the chart to be responsive.

### Add a Grid

Let's add a grid to the chart.



**Import the `CartesianGrid` component.**
**Add the `CartesianGrid` component to your chart.**

blocks.code:
<ChartContainer config={chartConfig} className="min-h-[200px] w-full">
  <BarChart accessibilityLayer data={chartData}>
    <CartesianGrid vertical={false} />
    <Bar dataKey="desktop" fill="var(--color-desktop)" radius={4} />
    <Bar dataKey="mobile" fill="var(--color-mobile)" radius={4} />
  </BarChart>
</ChartContainer>

blocks.text:
### Add an Axis

To add an x-axis to the chart, we'll use the `XAxis` component.



**Import the `XAxis` component.**

blocks.code: import { Bar, BarChart, CartesianGrid, XAxis } from "recharts"

blocks.text: **Add the `XAxis` component to your chart.**

blocks.code:
<ChartContainer config={chartConfig} className="h-[200px] w-full">
  <BarChart accessibilityLayer data={chartData}>
    <CartesianGrid vertical={false} />
    <XAxis
      dataKey="month"
      tickLine={false}
      tickMargin={10}
      axisLine={false}
      tickFormatter={(value) => value.slice(0, 3)}
    />
    <Bar dataKey="desktop" fill="var(--color-desktop)" radius={4} />
    <Bar dataKey="mobile" fill="var(--color-mobile)" radius={4} />
  </BarChart>
</ChartContainer>

blocks.text:
### Add Tooltip

So far we've only used components from Recharts. They look great out of the box thanks to some customization in the `chart` component.

To add a tooltip, we'll use the custom `ChartTooltip` and `ChartTooltipContent` components from `chart`.



**Import the `ChartTooltip` and `ChartTooltipContent` components.**
**Add the components to your chart.**

blocks.code:
<ChartContainer config={chartConfig} className="h-[200px] w-full">
  <BarChart accessibilityLayer data={chartData}>
    <CartesianGrid vertical={false} />
    <XAxis
      dataKey="month"
      tickLine={false}
      tickMargin={10}
      axisLine={false}
      tickFormatter={(value) => value.slice(0, 3)}
    />
    <ChartTooltip content={<ChartTooltipContent />} />
    <Bar dataKey="desktop" fill="var(--color-desktop)" radius={4} />
    <Bar dataKey="mobile" fill="var(--color-mobile)" radius={4} />
  </BarChart>
</ChartContainer>

blocks.text:
Hover to see the tooltips. Easy, right? Two components, and we've got a beautiful tooltip.


### Add Legend

We'll do the same for the legend. We'll use the `ChartLegend` and `ChartLegendContent` components from `chart`.



**Import the `ChartLegend` and `ChartLegendContent` components.**
**Add the components to your chart.**

blocks.code:
<ChartContainer config={chartConfig} className="h-[200px] w-full">
  <BarChart accessibilityLayer data={chartData}>
    <CartesianGrid vertical={false} />
    <XAxis
      dataKey="month"
      tickLine={false}
      tickMargin={10}
      axisLine={false}
      tickFormatter={(value) => value.slice(0, 3)}
    />
    <ChartTooltip content={<ChartTooltipContent />} />
    <ChartLegend content={<ChartLegendContent />} />
    <Bar dataKey="desktop" fill="var(--color-desktop)" radius={4} />
    <Bar dataKey="mobile" fill="var(--color-mobile)" radius={4} />
  </BarChart>
</ChartContainer>

blocks.text:
Done. You've built your first chart! What's next?

- [Themes and Colors](/docs/components/chart#theming)
- [Tooltip](/docs/components/chart#tooltip)
- [Legend](/docs/components/chart#legend)

## Chart Config

The chart config is where you define the labels, icons and colors for a chart.

It is intentionally decoupled from chart data.

This allows you to share config and color tokens between charts. It can also work independently for cases where your data or color tokens live remotely or in a different format.

## Theming

`CodeBlock` displays code, terminal output, logs and diffs. It has a header with a title and actions, line numbers, wrapping, diff and highlighted lines, and a small size for tool output in a [Trace](/docs/components/base/trace).

Syntax highlighting is optional and lives in a separate hook, so a block that only shows plain output stays small.

## Installation
cli
manual
**Install the following dependencies:**
**Install the required shadcn/ui dependencies:**
**Copy and paste the following code into your project.**

**Update the import paths to match your project setup.**





`code-block` also installs `useHighlightedCode` for [syntax highlighting](#syntax-highlighting).

## Usage

blocks.code:
import {
  CodeBlock,
  CodeBlockActions,
  CodeBlockContent,
  CodeBlockCopyButton,
  CodeBlockFooter,
  CodeBlockHeader,
  CodeBlockLine,
  CodeBlockTitle,
} from "@/components/ui/code-block"

blocks.text: ## Composition

blocks.code:
CodeBlock
├── CodeBlockHeader
│   ├── CodeBlockTitle
│   └── CodeBlockActions
│       └── CodeBlockCopyButton
├── CodeBlockActions (floating, when there is no header)
├── CodeBlockContent
│   └── CodeBlockLine
└── CodeBlockFooter

blocks.text:
`CodeBlockContent` takes a string or a list of `CodeBlockLine`. Use lines when you need line variants or highlighted tokens.

## Features

- **It streams cheaply.** A string child renders as one text node, and the highlighter tokenizes only the new lines as code arrives.
- **It copies cleanly.** Line numbers and diff markers are left out of a selection, and blank lines survive the copy.
- **It reads left to right.** The content is always `dir="ltr"`. The header follows the page direction.
- **It highlights without WASM.** `useHighlightedCode` uses Shiki's JavaScript engine, loads each language on first use and renders ANSI colors in terminal output. On the server, `highlightCode` keeps Shiki out of the client bundle.
- **It fits where code shows up.** Use it in a message, a Markdown fence, a Trace line, Tabs, a Dialog or a `typeset` container.
- **It scrolls by keyboard.** The content is focusable, and floating actions show on focus as well as on hover.

## Basic

Pass a string to `CodeBlockContent`. It renders as one text node, so it stays cheap while output streams.

## Header

`CodeBlockHeader` holds a `CodeBlockTitle` and `CodeBlockActions`. `CodeBlockCopyButton` copies its `value`.
A long title truncates. To link the title to a file, wrap `CodeBlockTitle` in an anchor.

## Actions

`CodeBlockActions` holds any number of buttons. For a wrap toggle, keep the state yourself and pass it to `wrap`.

blocks.code:
const [wrap, setWrap] = React.useState(false)

<CodeBlockActions>
  <Button
    variant="ghost"
    size="icon-xs"
    aria-label="Wrap lines"
    aria-pressed={wrap}
    onClick={() => setWrap(!wrap)}
  >
    <WrapTextIcon />
  </Button>
  <CodeBlockCopyButton value={output} />
</CodeBlockActions>
<CodeBlockContent wrap={wrap}>{output}</CodeBlockContent>

blocks.text:
## Floating Actions

Without a header, put `CodeBlockActions` directly inside `CodeBlock`. The actions float at the top end and stay hidden until the block is hovered or focused. They always show on touch screens.

## Line Numbers

Add `lineNumbers` to `CodeBlockContent`. A string child is split into lines, and the numbers are not copied with a selection.

## Start Line

Set `startLine` to number lines from a given line, for a snippet from the middle of a file. The gutter grows to fit the widest number.

## Wrap

Long lines scroll by default. Add `wrap` to wrap them, which suits tool output and error messages. To let the reader toggle it, see [Actions](#actions).

## Highlighted Lines

Render each line as a `CodeBlockLine` and set `variant="highlighted"` on the lines to call out.

## Diff

Set `variant="added"` or `variant="removed"` on a `CodeBlockLine`. Each one adds a `+` or `−` marker.

## Height

Cap the height with a `max-h-*` class on `CodeBlockContent`. The content scrolls inside the block.

`CodeBlockContent` fades its edges with [`scroll-fade`](/docs/utils/scroll-fade) as it scrolls: left and right by default, top and bottom when it wraps. Add `scroll-fade-y` to a capped block that does not wrap.

## Show More

`CodeBlockFooter` is a slot below the content. For Show More, cap the content while it is collapsed and put a ghost `xs` `Button` in the footer.

### Max Height

To keep a long block from taking over the page, raise the cap instead of removing it. The expanded content scrolls, and the edges fade as you scroll.

## Size

Use `size="sm"` for tool and [Trace](#trace) output. It has tighter padding and `text-xs` text.

## Destructive

Use `variant="destructive"` for errors and failed output.

## Trace

Put a `CodeBlock` with `size="sm"` in `TraceCollapsibleContent` for tool and terminal output. Add `wrap` and a `max-h-64` class to `CodeBlockContent` so long output wraps and scrolls inside the trace. The block sets its own text color, so `TraceCollapsibleContent` does not mute it.

## Tabs

Show several files with [Tabs](/docs/components/base/tabs), one `CodeBlock` in each `TabsContent`.

## Message

Put a `CodeBlock` between paragraphs inside a [Message](/docs/components/base/message).

## Typeset

A `CodeBlock` inside a [`typeset`](/docs/typeset) container keeps its own styles and gets the same space above as a paragraph.

## Syntax Highlighting

`useHighlightedCode` highlights with [Shiki](https://shiki.style) and returns one React node per line for `CodeBlockLine`.

Shiki uses its JavaScript regex engine, so there is no WASM to load.

### Languages

Each language loads the first time it is used. Edit the list in `lib/highlighter.tsx`. A language that is not in the list renders as plain text.

The list ships with `bash`, `css`, `diff`, `html`, `javascript`, `json`, `jsx`, `markdown`, `python`, `sql`, `tsx`, `typescript` and `yaml`, plus aliases such as `ts`, `js`, `sh` and `yml`.

### Terminal Output

Pass `"ansi"` as the language to render the colors in terminal output. Without it, escape codes show as text.

ANSI colors do not carry from one line to the next.

### Server Rendering

`highlightCode` is async and works in a Server Component, so Shiki stays out of the client bundle.

### Streaming

While the code streams, the hook tokenizes only the new lines, starting where the last line left off. Lines that did not change keep the same nodes, so React skips them.

### Markdown

Render the message with [Streamdown](https://streamdown.ai) and route fenced code to a `CodeBlock` with `components.code`. Streamdown sets `data-block` on fenced code only, so inline code stays inline.

`useIsCodeFenceIncomplete` returns `true` until the closing fence arrives. Use it to disable the copy button while the code is incomplete. It only works when Streamdown gets `isAnimating`, so pass `isAnimating` while the message streams.

## Accessibility

- `CodeBlockContent` is a `pre` with a `code` element and always sets `dir="ltr"`, so code reads left to right on an RTL page.
- `CodeBlockContent` has `tabIndex={0}`, so keyboard users can focus it and scroll it. Pass `tabIndex={-1}` to remove the tab stop.
- Floating actions show when focus is inside the block, not only on hover, so keyboard users can reach them.
- Line numbers are hidden from screen readers.
- Diff lines carry a `+` or `−` marker as well as a tint, so the change does not rely on color.
- `CodeBlockCopyButton` is labelled "Copy", and a polite live region announces "Copied" after a successful copy.
- Give a wrap toggle `aria-pressed` so its state is announced.
- Give a Show More button `aria-expanded` and point `aria-controls` at the `id` of `CodeBlockContent`.

## API Reference

### CodeBlock

The surface that holds the header, the content and the footer.

| Prop        | Type                         | Default     | Description                                                     |
| ----------- | ---------------------------- | ----------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `variant`   | `"default" \| "destructive"` | `"default"` | The tone of the block.                                          |
| `size`      | `"default" \| "sm"`          | `"default"` | `"sm"` has tighter padding and `text-xs` code, for tool output. |
| `className` | `string`                     | -           | Additional classes to apply to the block.                       |

### CodeBlockHeader

A row above the content for a title and actions.

| Prop        | Type     | Default | Description                                |
| ----------- | -------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| `className` | `string` | -       | Additional classes to apply to the header. |

### CodeBlockTitle

A filename or a label, with an optional icon. It truncates.

| Prop        | Type     | Default | Description                               |
| ----------- | -------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| `className` | `string` | -       | Additional classes to apply to the title. |

### CodeBlockActions

Holds buttons at the end of the header. As a direct child of `CodeBlock`, it floats.

| Prop        | Type     | Default | Description                                 |
| ----------- | -------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| `className` | `string` | -       | Additional classes to apply to the actions. |

### CodeBlockCopyButton

A ghost icon button that copies `value` to the clipboard. It accepts the props of [`Button`](/docs/components/base/button).

| Prop        | Type     | Default | Description                                |
| ----------- | -------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| `value`     | `string` | -       | Required. The text to copy.                |
| `className` | `string` | -       | Additional classes to apply to the button. |

### CodeBlockContent

The `pre` that scrolls or wraps.

| Prop          | Type              | Default | Description                                                     |
| ------------- | ----------------- | ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `children`    | `React.ReactNode` | -       | A string, or a list of `CodeBlockLine`.                         |
| `wrap`        | `boolean`         | `false` | Wrap long lines instead of scrolling.                           |
| `lineNumbers` | `boolean`         | `false` | Number each line. A string child is split into lines.           |
| `startLine`   | `number`          | `1`     | The number of the first line, when `lineNumbers` is set.        |
| `tabIndex`    | `number`          | `0`     | Makes the content focusable so it can be scrolled by keyboard.  |
| `className`   | `string`          | -       | Additional classes to apply to the content, such as `max-h-72`. |

### CodeBlockLine

One line of code.

| Prop        | Type                                                 | Default     | Description                              |
| ----------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | ----------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| `variant`   | `"default" \| "added" \| "removed" \| "highlighted"` | `"default"` | The state of the line.                   |
| `className` | `string`                                             | -           | Additional classes to apply to the line. |

### CodeBlockFooter

A row below the content, such as for a Show More button.

| Prop        | Type     | Default | Description                                |
| ----------- | -------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| `className` | `string` | -       | Additional classes to apply to the footer. |

### useHighlightedCode

Returns one React node per line. It returns plain lines until the first pass finishes, and for a language that is not in the list.

| Argument   | Type     | Description                                                  |
| ---------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `code`     | `string` | The code to highlight. A trailing newline is ignored.        |
| `language` | `string` | A language or alias from `lib/highlighter.tsx`, or `"ansi"`. |

title: Data Table
description: Powerful table and datagrids built using TanStack Table.

blocks.text:
## Introduction

Every data table or datagrid I've created has been unique. They all behave differently, have specific sorting and filtering requirements, and work with different data sources.

It doesn't make sense to combine all of these variations into a single component. If we do that, we'll lose the flexibility that [headless UI](https://tanstack.com/table/latest/docs/overview#what-is-headless-ui) provides.

So instead of a data-table component, I thought it would be more helpful to provide a guide on how to build your own.

We'll start with the basic `<Table />` component and build a complex data table from scratch.
**Tip:** If you find yourself using the same table in multiple places in your app, you can always extract it into a reusable component.

## Table of Contents

This guide will show you how to use [TanStack Table](https://tanstack.com/table) and the `<Table />` component to build your own custom data table. We'll cover the following topics:

- [Set up Table Features](#set-up-table-features)
- [Basic Table](#basic-table)
- [Row Actions](#row-actions)
- [Pagination](#pagination)
- [Sorting](#sorting)
- [Filtering](#filtering)
- [Visibility](#visibility)
- [Row Selection](#row-selection)
- [Reusable Components](#reusable-components)

## Installation

1. Add the `<Table />` component to your project:
2. Add the `@tanstack/react-table` dependency. This guide uses **TanStack Table v9**:

## Prerequisites

We are going to build a table to show recent payments. Here's what our data looks like:

## Project Structure

Start by creating the following file structure:

blocks.code:
app
└── payments
    ├── columns.tsx
    ├── data-table-features.ts
    ├── data-table.tsx
    └── page.tsx

blocks.text:
I'm using a Next.js example here but this works for any other React framework.

- `columns.tsx` (client component) will contain our column definitions.
- `data-table-features.ts` will contain the shared `features` object that tells TanStack Table which behavior to enable.
- `data-table.tsx` (client component) will contain our `<DataTable />` component.
- `page.tsx` (server component) is where we'll fetch data and render our table.

## Set up Table Features

TanStack Table v9 is feature-based: you opt into the behavior you want — sorting, filtering, pagination, and so on — by declaring it with `tableFeatures()`. Anything you don't list is tree-shaken out of your bundle. That includes the built-in filter and sort functions: register the ones your columns rely on under `filterFns` and `sortFns` (our email filter uses `includesString`, and string columns sort with `text` / `alphanumeric`).

blocks.title: app/payments/data-table-features.ts
blocks.code:
import {
  columnFilteringFeature,
  columnVisibilityFeature,
  createFilteredRowModel,
  createPaginatedRowModel,
  createSortedRowModel,
  filterFn_includesString,
  rowPaginationFeature,
  rowSelectionFeature,
  rowSortingFeature,
  sortFn_alphanumeric,
  sortFn_text,
  tableFeatures,
} from "@tanstack/react-table"

// New in v9: declare the features this table uses — anything you don't
// register is tree-shaken out of the bundle.
export const features = tableFeatures({
  columnFilteringFeature,
  columnVisibilityFeature,
  rowPaginationFeature,
  rowSelectionFeature,
  rowSortingFeature,
  filteredRowModel: createFilteredRowModel(),
  paginatedRowModel: createPaginatedRowModel(),
  sortedRowModel: createSortedRowModel(),
  filterFns: { includesString: filterFn_includesString },
  sortFns: { alphanumeric: sortFn_alphanumeric, text: sortFn_text },
})

// Pass this as the first generic argument to `ColumnDef`, `Column`, `Table`,
// and `Row` so each type knows which feature APIs are available.
export type DataTableFeatures = typeof features

blocks.text: **Note:** The core row model is always included, so you never register it yourself. Row models for optional features are created with `create*RowModel()` and registered on the features object — there are no more `get*RowModel` table options.

## Basic Table

Let's start by building a basic table.


### Column Definitions

First, we'll define our columns.

blocks.title: app/payments/columns.tsx

blocks.text:
**Note:** Columns are where you define the core of what your table
will look like. They define the data that will be displayed, how it will be
formatted, sorted and filtered.

### `<DataTable />` component

Next, we'll create a `<DataTable />` component to render our table.

blocks.title: app/payments/data-table.tsx

blocks.text:
**Tip**: If you find yourself using `<DataTable />` in multiple places, this is the component you could make reusable by extracting it to `components/ui/data-table.tsx`.

title: Dialog
description: A sheet over the page. A drawer rising from the bottom on a phone, a dialog popping up from its centre on a computer.

blocks.text: ## Installation
manual
**Install the following dependencies. The dialog has no state and no ``use client``, so it renders on the server.**
**Copy and paste the following code into your project. It uses the [Button](/docs/button).**

**Add the `--scrim` and `--sheet-shadow` tokens and the `dialog-overlay` / `dialog-content` motion rules to your CSS file. They are in `app/globals.css`.**





## Usage

blocks.code:
import {
  Dialog,
  DialogClose,
  DialogContent,
  DialogDescription,
  DialogFooter,
  DialogHeader,
  DialogTitle,
  DialogTrigger,
} from "@/components/ui/dialog"

<Dialog>
  <DialogTrigger>Open</DialogTrigger>
  <DialogContent>
    <DialogHeader>
      <DialogTitle>Remove this device?</DialogTitle>
      <DialogDescription>
        The router will forget its key.
      </DialogDescription>
    </DialogHeader>
    <DialogFooter>
      <DialogClose>Cancel</DialogClose>
      <Button variant="red">Remove</Button>
    </DialogFooter>
  </DialogContent>
</Dialog>

blocks.text:
## Composition

Use the following composition to build a `Dialog`:

blocks.code:
Dialog
├── DialogTrigger
└── DialogContent
    ├── DialogHeader
    │   ├── DialogTitle
    │   └── DialogDescription
    ├── (your content)
    └── DialogFooter

blocks.text:
## A question

The sheet asks in the way iOS does: the title and a short paragraph on the left, then two equal buttons. **Cancel** is `soft` and the action is `accent` (or `red` for a removal). There is no × beside them, so leave `showCloseButton` on only when the dialog has more than a choice.

## Form

Fields sit between the header and the footer. The footer buttons share the width.

## With a close button

`showCloseButton` is on by default: a 32px round knob pinned at the top right, 22px from the edges. The header makes room for it.

## Sticky footer

Keep the actions in view while the content scrolls.

## Scrollable content

Long content scrolls inside the sheet. The sheet never grows past the screen: it stops 16px from the edges.

## Design

- **Shape.** The `raised` surface (`card`) with a 36px radius, 24px padding and the sheet shadow. No border and no ring.
- **Title.** 20/28 at 500 with -0.5px tracking. The description is 14/20 in the secondary text colour.
- **Phone (below 760px).** A drawer floating 16px off the left, right and bottom edges (safe areas included), at most 400px wide. It rises 500ms on the drawer curve (`cubic-bezier(.32,.72,0,1)`) and leaves in 420ms. The scrim fades in 420ms and out in 320ms.
- **Computer (760px and up).** Centred by layout, with inset and auto margins, so the text stays on the pixel grid. It pops up from its centre: `scale .9 → 1` and `blur 4px → 0` on the soft spring in 476ms. It leaves in 120ms ease-in to `scale .96` and `blur 3px`.
- **Scrim.** 80% black in dark, 62% light in light. It only dims: nothing is blurred behind the sheet.
- **Closes by** ×, the scrim or Escape.
- **Reduced motion.** Travel and scale drop out and the fades shorten.

## API Reference

| Part | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `Dialog` | The root. Controlled with `open` and `onOpenChange`, or `defaultOpen`. |
| `DialogTrigger` | Opens the dialog. Draw it as another element with `render`. |
| `DialogContent` | The sheet and its scrim. `showCloseButton` (default `true`) shows the round ×. |
| `DialogHeader`, `DialogTitle`, `DialogDescription` | The head. The title names the dialog for screen readers. |
| `DialogFooter` | A row of equal buttons. `showCloseButton` adds a soft Close button before the others. |
| `DialogClose` | Closes the dialog. Draw it as a `Button` with `render`. |

See the [Base UI](https://base-ui.com/react/components/dialog#api-reference) documentation for the rest.

The drawer component now uses [Base

## Installation

## Usage

blocks.code:
import {
  Drawer,
  DrawerClose,
  DrawerContent,
  DrawerDescription,
  DrawerFooter,
  DrawerHeader,
  DrawerTitle,
  DrawerTrigger,
} from "@/components/ui/drawer"

}>Open Are you absolutely sure? This action cannot be undone.
{/* Content here */}
}>Cancel

blocks.text:
## Composition

Use the following composition to build a `Drawer`:

blocks.code:
Drawer
├── DrawerTrigger
└── DrawerContent
    ├── DrawerHeader
    │   ├── DrawerTitle
    │   └── DrawerDescription
    └── DrawerFooter

blocks.text:
`DrawerContent` composes the portal, overlay, viewport, and popup from Base UI. For lower-level control, `DrawerPortal`, `DrawerOverlay`, and `DrawerSwipeHandle` are also exported.

## Custom Sizes

A vertical drawer sizes itself to its content and is capped at `calc(100dvh - 6rem)` by default. A side drawer spans `75%` of the viewport width, or `24rem` on larger screens.

To customize the height of a vertical drawer, use the `h-*` and `max-h-*` utilities on `DrawerContent`.
To customize the width of a side drawer, use the `w-*` and `max-w-*` utilities on `DrawerContent`.
When the same component renders in multiple directions, scope an override to one axis using the `data-[swipe-axis=*]` variants.
To make a region of the drawer scrollable, make the scroll container a flex item. Avoid `h-full`, which does not resolve inside a content-sized drawer.

## Styling

The drawer exposes CSS variables for style-level customization. Set the sizing variables on `DrawerContent`. Set the overlay variable on `[data-slot=drawer-overlay]` in your CSS.

| Variable                       | Default                | Description                                                             |
| ------------------------------ | ---------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--drawer-inset`               | `0px`                  | Floats the drawer from the viewport edges.                              |
| `--drawer-bleed-background`    | `var(--color-popover)` | Fills the gap behind the drawer on swipe overshoot.                     |
| `--drawer-overlay-min-opacity` | `0`                    | Minimum overlay opacity. Defaults to `0.5` when snap points are active. |

The drawer also sets data attributes you can target with variants such as `data-[swipe-direction=down]:` on `DrawerContent`, or `group-data-[swipe-axis=y]/drawer-popup:` on its descendants.

| Attribute                 | Values                        | Set when                              |
| ------------------------- | ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| `data-swipe-direction`    | `up`, `right`, `down`, `left` | Always.                               |
| `data-swipe-axis`         | `x`, `y`                      | Always.                               |
| `data-snap-points`        | Present                       | The drawer has snap points.           |
| `data-expanded`           | Present                       | The drawer is at the full snap point. |
| `data-swiping`            | Present                       | A swipe is in progress.               |
| `data-nested-drawer-open` | Present                       | A nested drawer is open on top.       |

## Position

Use the `swipeDirection` prop to set the side of the drawer.

Available options are `up`, `right`, `down`, and `left`.

## Swipe Handle

Use `showSwipeHandle` on `Drawer` to render a swipe handle.

## Nested

Open drawers from inside another drawer. Parent drawers stay mounted and stack behind the frontmost drawer.

## Non Modal

Set `modal={false}` to allow interaction with the rest of the page while the drawer is open. Combine with `disablePointerDismissal` to prevent the drawer from closing on outside presses. Use `modal="trap-focus"` to keep focus inside the drawer while leaving scroll and pointer interaction unrestricted.

## Snap Points

Use `snapPoints` to snap a drawer to preset heights. Numbers between `0` and `1` represent fractions of the viewport. Numbers greater than `1` are treated as pixel values. String values support `px` and `rem` units. Snap points apply to vertical drawers.

Track the active snap point with the controlled `snapPoint` and `onSnapPointChange` props. At the full snap point, the drawer gets a `data-expanded` attribute you can style with the `data-expanded:` variant.

## Responsive

You can combine the `Dialog` and `Drawer` components to create a responsive dialog. This renders a `Dialog` component on desktop and a `Drawer` on mobile.

## Migrating from Vaul

The base drawer now uses [Base UI](https://base-ui.com/react/components/drawer)
instead of Vaul. If you installed the previous base drawer, update your usage
to the Base UI API.



**Update the dependency.**

**Replace `direction` with `swipeDirection`.**


Use `down` instead of `bottom`, and `up` instead of `top`. `left` and `right`
stay the same.

**Replace `asChild` with `render`.**


For `DrawerTrigger`, pass the trigger element to the `render` prop.
For `DrawerClose`, pass the close element to the `render` prop.

**Update snap point props.**


If you use snap points, rename the controlled snap point props and the sequential
snap point prop.

blocks.code:
<Drawer
    snapPoints={[0.25, 0.5, 1]}
-   activeSnapPoint={snapPoint}
-   setActiveSnapPoint={setSnapPoint}
-   snapToSequentialPoint
+   snapPoint={snapPoint}
+   onSnapPointChange={setSnapPoint}
+   snapToSequentialPoints
  >

blocks.text: **Update animation and focus props.**

**Review Vaul-only props.**


Vaul props like `handleOnly`, `repositionInputs`, and
`shouldScaleBackground` do not have one-to-one replacements in the base drawer
API. Use Base UI props such as `disablePointerDismissal`, `modal`, `snapPoints`,
or controlled `open` state for the behavior you need.

**Update custom data attribute selectors.**


Replace Vaul's `data-vaul-drawer-direction` selectors with Base UI's
`data-swipe-direction` selectors.

Base UI also exposes attributes like `data-swiping`, `data-starting-style`, and
`data-ending-style` for swipe and transition states. Descendants inside
`DrawerContent` can use `group-data-[swipe-axis=x]/drawer-popup` and
`group-data-[swipe-axis=y]/drawer-popup` for axis-specific styling.


## API Reference

See the [Base UI documentation](https://base-ui.com/react/components/drawer) for the full API reference.

## Composition

blocks.code:
DropdownMenu
├── DropdownMenuTrigger
└── DropdownMenuContent
    ├── DropdownMenuGroup
    │   ├── DropdownMenuLabel
    │   ├── DropdownMenuItem
    │   │   └── DropdownMenuText
    │   │       └── DropdownMenuDescription
    │   └── DropdownMenuItem
    ├── DropdownMenuSeparator
    ├── DropdownMenuCheckboxItem
    ├── DropdownMenuRadioGroup
    │   └── DropdownMenuRadioItem
    └── DropdownMenuSub
        ├── DropdownMenuSubTrigger
        └── DropdownMenuSubContent

blocks.text:
## Basic

A menu with a label, a separator and a disabled row.

## Icons

An icon goes before the words. It is 16px, 14px in from the rounded edge, and grows to 1.08 under the highlight.

## A line under the label

Wrap the label and `DropdownMenuDescription` in `DropdownMenuText`. The row grows from 34px to 50px. The line is 11.5px with tabular figures, good for an address.

## Variants

`warn` is for an action with a cost, like Reconnect. `destructive` is for one that cannot be undone, like Remove. The highlight is the same for both: only the text changes colour. See the demo at the top.

## Shortcuts
## Submenu
## Checkboxes
## Radio group

## Design

- **Glass.** Apple's iOS 26 Liquid Glass (Regular): on dark black 40% with a white 4% film, on light `rgba(245,245,245,.6)`. Backdrop `blur 28px`, `saturate 1.8`, and a soft inner 1px edge (`--glass-edge`). Dark has no shadow, light has a soft one. Nothing dims around it.
- **Shape.** At least 210px wide, radius 24, padding 6. Rows are 34px high, radius 18 (concentric with the glass), 14px in at the left and 12px at the right. The label is 14/18 at 400.
- **Separators.** 13px high with a 1px line 16px in from the edges.
- **Placement.** Centred on its button, 8px away, under it where it fits and over it where it does not, and 12px inside the screen's edge.
- **Open.** Grows out of its button: `scale .5 → 1` and `blur 6px → 0` on the soft spring (476ms, about 4% over), from the side it hangs off.
- **Close.** Goes back towards the button in 110ms ease-in to `scale .7` and `blur 4px`: quicker than it came.
- **Highlight.** One for all the rows, under their icons and words, the same solid for every row. It fades in (160ms, ease-out) where the pointer or the keyboard is and glides from row to row on the glide spring (about 2% over): place, size and corners. A press takes it to 0.97 with its row, and it fades where the pointer leaves the rows. Back on a row while it still fades, it turns back and glides from where it stands. The icon under it grows to 1.08.
- **Closes by** a press outside, the trigger again, Escape or a choice.

The glide is moved by `MenuGlide`, a small client component that listens on the document, so the menu itself stays a server component. The menu holds one empty `<span data-slot="dropdown-menu-highlight">` for it. Without `MenuGlide` the row under the pointer lights up by itself.

## API Reference

| Part | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `DropdownMenu` | The root. Controlled with `open` and `onOpenChange`, or `defaultOpen`. |
| `DropdownMenuTrigger` | Opens the menu. Draw it as a `Button` with `render`. |
| `DropdownMenuContent` | The glass. `side`, `align` (default `center`), `sideOffset` (8) and `collisionPadding` (12). |
| `DropdownMenuItem` | A row. `variant` is `"default"`, `"warn"` or `"destructive"`. |
| `DropdownMenuText`, `DropdownMenuDescription` | A label with a line under it. |
| `DropdownMenuCheckboxItem`, `DropdownMenuRadioItem` | A row with a check on the right. |
| `DropdownMenuSub`, `DropdownMenuSubTrigger`, `DropdownMenuSubContent` | A submenu. |
| `DropdownMenuLabel`, `DropdownMenuSeparator`, `DropdownMenuShortcut` | Caption, divider and key hint. |

See the [Base UI](https://base-ui.com/react/components/menu#api-reference) documentation for the rest.

- `Field` is the core wrapper for a single field.
- `FieldContent` is a flex column that groups label and description. Not required if you have no description.
- Wrap related fields with `FieldGroup`, and use `FieldSet` with `FieldLegend` for semantic grouping.

## Form

See the [Form](/docs/forms) documentation for building forms with the `Field` component and [React Hook Form](/docs/forms/react-hook-form), [Tanstack Form](/docs/forms/tanstack-form), or [Formisch](/docs/forms/formisch).

## Input
## Textarea
## Select
## Slider
## Fieldset
## Checkbox
## Radio
## Switch

## Choice Card

Wrap `Field` components inside `FieldLabel` to create selectable field groups. This works with `RadioItem`, `Checkbox` and `Switch` components.

## Field Group

Stack `Field` components with `FieldGroup`. Add `FieldSeparator` to divide them.

## Responsive Layout

- **Vertical fields:** Default orientation stacks label, control, and helper text—ideal for mobile-first layouts.
- **Horizontal fields:** Set `orientation="horizontal"` on `Field` to align the label and control side-by-side. Pair with `FieldContent` to keep descriptions aligned.
- **Responsive fields:** Set `orientation="responsive"` for automatic column layouts inside container-aware parents. Apply `@container/field-group` classes on `FieldGroup` to switch orientations at specific breakpoints.

## Validation and Errors

- Add `data-invalid` to `Field` to switch the entire block into an error state.
- Add `aria-invalid` on the input itself for assistive technologies.
- Render `FieldError` immediately after the control or inside `FieldContent` to keep error messages aligned with the field.

blocks.code:
<Field data-invalid>
  <FieldLabel htmlFor="email">Email</FieldLabel>
  <Input id="email" type="email" aria-invalid />
  <FieldError>Enter a valid email address.</FieldError>
</Field>

blocks.text:
## Accessibility

- `FieldSet` and `FieldLegend` keep related controls grouped for keyboard and assistive tech users.
- `Field` outputs `role="group"` so nested controls inherit labeling from `FieldLabel` and `FieldLegend` when combined.
- Apply `FieldSeparator` sparingly to ensure screen readers encounter clear section boundaries.

## API Reference

### FieldSet

Container that renders a semantic `fieldset` with spacing presets.

| Prop        | Type     | Default |
| ----------- | -------- | ------- |
| `className` | `string` |         |

### FieldLegend

Legend element for a `FieldSet`. Switch to the `label` variant to align with label sizing.

| Prop        | Type                  | Default    |
| ----------- | --------------------- | ---------- |
| `variant`   | `"legend" \| "label"` | `"legend"` |
| `className` | `string`              |            |

The `FieldLegend` has two variants: `legend` and `label`. The `label` variant applies label sizing and alignment. Handy if you have nested `FieldSet`.

### FieldGroup

Layout wrapper that stacks `Field` components and enables container queries for responsive orientations.

| Prop        | Type     | Default |
| ----------- | -------- | ------- |
| `className` | `string` |         |

### Field

The core wrapper for a single field. Provides orientation control, invalid state styling, and spacing.

| Prop           | Type                                         | Default      |
| -------------- | -------------------------------------------- | ------------ |
| `orientation`  | `"vertical" \| "horizontal" \| "responsive"` | `"vertical"` |
| `className`    | `string`                                     |              |
| `data-invalid` | `boolean`                                    |              |

### FieldContent

Flex column that groups control and descriptions when the label sits beside the control. Not required if you have no description.

| Prop        | Type     | Default |
| ----------- | -------- | ------- |
| `className` | `string` |         |

### FieldLabel

Label styled for both direct inputs and nested `Field` children.

| Prop        | Type     | Default |
| ----------- | -------- | ------- |
| `className` | `string` |         |

### FieldTitle

Renders a title with label styling inside `FieldContent`.

| Prop        | Type     | Default |
| ----------- | -------- | ------- |
| `className` | `string` |         |

### FieldDescription

Helper text slot that automatically balances long lines in horizontal layouts.

| Prop        | Type     | Default |
| ----------- | -------- | ------- |
| `className` | `string` |         |

blocks.code: <FieldDescription>We never share your email with anyone.</FieldDescription>

blocks.text:
### FieldSeparator

Visual divider to separate sections inside a `FieldGroup`. Accepts optional inline content.

| Prop        | Type     | Default |
| ----------- | -------- | ------- |
| `className` | `string` |         |

### FieldError

Accessible error container that accepts children or an `errors` array (e.g., from `react-hook-form`).

| Prop        | Type                                       | Default |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------------ | ------- |
| `errors`    | `Array<{ message?: string } \| undefined>` |         |
| `className` | `string`                                   |         |

When the `errors` array contains multiple messages, the component renders a list automatically.

`FieldError` also accepts issues produced by any validator that implements [Standard Schema](https://standardschema.dev/), including Zod, Valibot, and ArkType. Pass the `issues` array from the schema result directly to render a unified error list across libraries.

## Usage

import { GlassIcon } from "@/components/ui/glass-icon"

blocks.text:
## Any Lucide icon

Pass the icon component itself, not an element, to `icon`. Every icon in [Lucide](https://lucide.dev/icons) works: the glass is the same, and the icon is drawn on it as a white detail line.

The icon sits on a frosted square with a tinted circle behind it. Its line keeps the same weight whatever the size of the glass.

## Tones

The tone is state, as everywhere in the kit. `grey` is the neutral one, `blue` is the accent or a plain choice, `green` is fine, `orange` needs attention and `red` is an end or a removal.

## Size

The size is set with the CSS size utilities, so the glass scales without blurring. Good sizes are 22 and 24 in rows, 32 on cards, 36 in notices, 44 and 56 on empty states and 64 in questions.

## In other components

A glass icon goes where a notice, a row or a question needs a mark: the media of an [Alert](/docs/alert), an [Alert Dialog](/docs/alert-dialog) or an Item.

## Drawn shapes

The built-in icons have a back shape and a pane drawn for each, so the pane follows the object: a phone, a router, a shield. Use them with `name` when the object is one of these.

## Design

- **Glass.** A tinted back shape, the same shape blurred behind a frosted pane, a thin rim and a white detail. The colours are the `--t-*` and `--gi-*` tokens, so they change with the theme.
- **Lucide.** The pane is the `other` shape, a 14 unit square with a radius of 3.6 and a circle behind its top right corner. The icon is 9 units wide in the middle of the pane, with a stroke of 4 on the 24 unit grid, which is 1.5 at the size drawn.
- **Hidden from readers.** The icon is decoration (`aria-hidden`). Put the meaning in the text beside it.

## API Reference

| Prop | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `icon` | `LucideIcon`. Any Lucide icon. Use either `icon` or `name`. | - |
| `name` | One of the drawn shapes: `phone`, `mobile`, `tablet`, `computer`, `router`, `other`, `plus`, `globe`, `home`, `shield`, `chart`, `calendar`, `clock`, `lock`, `check`, `trash`, `refresh`. | - |
| `tone` | `"grey" \| "blue" \| "green" \| "orange" \| "red"` | `"grey"` |
| `className` | Use `size-*` for the size. | - |

blocks.text:
The `Marker` component displays inline conversation markers such as status updates, system notes, bordered rows, and labeled separators. Compose it with [`Message`](/docs/components/message) in a conversation thread.

## Installation
cli
manual
**Copy and paste the following code into your project.**

**Update the import paths to match your project setup.**





## Usage

## Composition

Use the following composition to build a marker:

## Features

- Inline marker, bordered row, and labeled separator variants
- Decorative icon slot that is hidden from assistive tech
- Polymorphic root via `render` for link and button markers
- Pairs with the [`shimmer`](/docs/utils/shimmer) utility for streaming status text
- Customizable styling through the `className` prop on every part

## Variants

Use `variant` to switch between an inline marker, bordered row, and labeled separator.

| Variant     | Description                                          |
| ----------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `default`   | An inline marker for status, notes, and actions.     |
| `border`    | A default marker with a bottom border under the row. |
| `separator` | A centered label with divider lines on each side.    |

## Status

Set `role="status"` and include a [`Spinner`](/docs/components/spinner) for streaming or in-progress markers so updates are announced.

## Shimmer

Add the [`shimmer`](/docs/utils/shimmer) utility class to `MarkerContent` for an animated streaming-text effect. The utility ships with the `shadcn` package — see the shimmer docs for installation.

## Separator

Use the `separator` variant for labeled dividers, such as dates or section breaks, in a conversation. A [Checkpoint](/docs/ai-elements/base/checkpoint) is a separator with a button that restores the thread to that point.

## Border

Use the `border` variant for status rows that should keep the default marker alignment while separating the next row.

## With Icon

Use `MarkerIcon` to render an icon alongside the content. Use `flex-col` to stack the icon above the content.

## Links and Buttons

Turn a marker into a link or button with the `render` prop on `Marker`.

## Accessibility

`Marker` is presentational by default. The correct semantics depend on how you use it, so choose the role based on intent rather than relying on a single default.

### Status and Progress

For streaming or progress markers such as "Thinking..." or a running tool, set `role="status"` so assistive tech announces the update as it appears. `Marker` forwards `role` to the underlying element.

### Labeled Separators

A separator that carries text, such as a date or a section label, needs no role. The divider lines are decorative CSS pseudo-elements, and the text is announced as ordinary content.

**Note:** Do not add `role="separator"` to a labeled divider. A separator
  takes its accessible name from `aria-label`, not from its text, and its
  contents are treated as presentational, so the visible label would not be
  announced. Reserve `role="separator"` for a divider with no meaningful text.

### Bordered Markers

A bordered marker keeps the same semantics as the default marker. The bottom border is decorative, so choose `role="status"`, `render`, or no role based on the marker's purpose.

### Decorative Icons

`MarkerIcon` is decorative and hidden from assistive tech with `aria-hidden`, so the adjacent `MarkerContent` carries the meaning. For an icon-only marker, provide an `aria-label` or visible text so it is not announced as empty.

### Interactive Markers

When a marker links or triggers an action, render it as a real `<button>` or `<a>` with the `render` prop so it is focusable and exposes the correct role. The accessible name comes from the marker text.

## API Reference

### Marker

The root marker element. The file also exports `markerVariants` for composing the marker styles into custom components.

| Prop        | Type                                   | Default     | Description                                      |
| ----------- | -------------------------------------- | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| `variant`   | `"default" \| "border" \| "separator"` | `"default"` | The marker layout.                               |
| `render`    | `ReactElement \| function`             | -           | Render as a different element, such as a link.   |
| `className` | `string`                               | -           | Additional classes to apply to the root element. |

### MarkerIcon

A decorative icon slot. Hidden from assistive tech with `aria-hidden`.

| Prop        | Type     | Default | Description                                   |
| ----------- | -------- | ------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| `className` | `string` | -       | Additional classes to apply to the icon slot. |

### MarkerContent

The marker text content.

| Prop        | Type     | Default | Description                                      |
| ----------- | -------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| `className` | `string` | -       | Additional classes to apply to the content slot. |

The `Message` component lays out a single message in a conversation. It handles the avatar, alignment, header, and footer around the message surface.

For AI apps, you can render reasoning steps, tool calls and assistant messages using the `Message` component.

## Installation
cli
manual

## Usage

blocks.code:
import { Avatar, AvatarFallback, AvatarImage } from "@/components/ui/avatar"
import { Bubble, BubbleContent } from "@/components/ui/bubble"
import { Message, MessageAvatar, MessageContent } from "@/components/ui/message"

<Message>
  <MessageAvatar>
    <Avatar>
      <AvatarImage src="https://github.com/shadcn.png" alt="@shadcn" />
      <AvatarFallback>CN</AvatarFallback>
    </Avatar>
  </MessageAvatar>
  <MessageContent>
    <Bubble>
      <BubbleContent>How can I help you today?</BubbleContent>
    </Bubble>

blocks.text:
**Note:** `Message` owns the row layout—avatar, alignment, header, and footer.
Render the visible message surface inside it with
[`Bubble`](/docs/components/bubble). For the scroll container around a
conversation, use [`MessageScroller`](/docs/components/message-scroller).
